| `IBSS-CLK-006` — The routine at 0x8400e034 (gate index in r0) is a reset pulse: only for gates 0x23, 0x26, 0x27 and 0x2e (mask 0x819 applied to index - 0x23) it sets bit 31 of the gate word, calls the delay routine 0x8400edac with 1, and clears bit 31. Its only caller (0x8400fe00) takes a controller index 0 or 1, uses gate 0x26 + index, and for anything else logs "WMR_CLOCK_RESET_DEVICE called with invalid FMI"; its sibling at 0x8400fe28 calls the single-gate routine with the same 0x26 + index. WMR is Apple's NAND flash translation layer and FMI the flash controller, and OpeniBoot names the same gates H2FMI0_CLOCK_GATE 0x26 and H2FMI1_CLOCK_GATE 0x27. So physical gate 0x27 is the NAND controller 1. The device tree's clock-gates value for the iop node is also 0x27; the project's STAGE 28 read of 0xF therefore says the NAND controller 1 clock was on, and says nothing about the IOP's clock. | `IBSS-GPIO-001` — The routine takes a pin id (port in bits 15 to 8, pin in bits 2 to 0) and a mode 0 to 7. For port 0x2e it calls another function. It computes new = (old AND NOT mask) OR (value AND mask) with, per mode: 0 value 0x210 mask 0x27e; 1 value 0x212 mask 0x27e; 2 value 0x212 mask 0x27f; 3 value 0x213 mask 0x27f; 5 value 0x230 mask 0x27e; 6 value 0x250 mask 0x27e; 7 value 0x270 mask 0x27e; and mode 4 takes the value from the table below with mask 0x3ff. | `IBSS-GPIO-002` — Mode 4 reads a 16-bit entry at 0x84017690 + 2 * index (index = 8 * port + pin) and uses its low ten bits: a table of per-pad default configurations (376 entries read here). ## Open links and hardware tests

Open links are the places where a reconstructed control-flow graph stops: an indirect or external call, an unknown producer, a register meaning. `complete` on a fiche covers its own instructions only, never what these links lead to. Hardware tests are listed with their own status, including results that contradicted the reading.

| Open link | Function | What is unknown | Proof needed |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ARM7M-ADDR-Q1` | `addr_adjust_by_version (working name, not Apple's)` | What the argument and the result are (an address in which address space, and whether -1 means failure), and who calls this method. The decoding is confirmed by the bytes (cmp r1,r0; it lo; mov.w r1,-1: an unsigned comparison, replacement when r1 < r0, as ARM defines LO). What is odd is the behaviour: for iop-version 1 the result is replaced by -1 when the offset is BELOW the size, which is not an ordinary range check. The condition is not to be inverted to fit a presumed name. Host side (EMBIOP-SEQ-006): slot +0x35c of AppleARM7M's table at 0x8071409c is this method (verified: the word at 0x8071409c+0x35c is 0x80713021), and EmbeddedIOP calls that slot on its provider with the slot-+0x98 result of each IOP-visible allocation. So the argument is, by its use, a physical address and the result an address in the IOP's view. Reading of the numbers, unverified: 0x40000000 would be the RAM base, and -1 would mark an address inside the window [0, size) where the IOP sees the firmware image. | read how EmbeddedIOP treats a -1 result of the slot +0x35c call |

This is the byte value only; no direction, polarity or electrical state is concluded from it, and the layout was not tested by changing the register. |
| trace_pmu_w34 (STAGE 39), write of register 0x50 | `setGPIOFunction (the driver's own message says '_setGPIOFunction')` | executed | Register 0x50 read 0x11 and was written 0x13 (= (0x11 & 0x19) | 0x02), acknowledged, read back 0x13, still 0x13 20 ms later, then written back 0x11 and read 0x11. This tests that the PMU takes the rebuilt byte; it does not test the polarity, the pin's electrical state or what the pin gates, and not that the touch driver writes this value (only that this is what the code computes). |
| trace_pmu_read (STAGE 36), registers 0x10 and 0x11 | `setLDO (working name; the driver's own log text says '_setLDO')` | executed | 0x10 = 0xEB and 0x11 = 0xBE were read, so bit 0x40 of 0x11 is clear. This is consistent with the LDO being off, under the rule that a set bit means on, which comes from this code and was not verified by switching anything. |
| trace_pmu_w34 (STAGE 39), write of bit 0x40 of register 0x11 | `setLDO (working name; the driver's own log text says '_setLDO')` | executed | With the explicit go of the person holding the phone: 0x11 read 0xBE, was written 0xFE (acknowledged), read back 0xFE, still 0xFE 20 ms later, then written back 0xBE and read 0xBE. The PMU accepts and keeps the write. Nothing was observed about the rail itself: whether bit 0x40 is the touch controller's supply was not tested, and no consumer was exercised. |

The table is therefore an initial configuration, not the state at the survey. |
